sftp.lan-only-note: SFTP is served on your local network and is not published through the Livinity (Cloudflare) tunnel. Whether it can be reached from the internet depends on your own router and firewall settings.
sftp.windows-step: On Windows, use a client such as WinSCP or FileZilla with the SFTP address and your LivOS username and password.
sftp.macos-step: On macOS, use a client such as Cyberduck, or run sftp from the Terminal, with the SFTP address and your LivOS username and password.
sftp.linux-step: On Linux, use the sftp command or sshfs with the SFTP address and your LivOS username and password.

net-expose.title: Ports
net-expose.description: Open managed TCP/UDP ports to the internet for a specific app or service.
net-expose.admin-only: Only an administrator can manage port openings.
net-expose.unavailable: Port management is not available on this device yet.
net-expose.wsl2-note: This device runs inside WSL2, where inbound networking is managed by the Windows host. Port openings are configured in Windows, not here.
net-expose.note-nat: Your router must still forward this port to this device (NAT). That is a separate step outside LivOS.
net-expose.note-ufw: These openings live in the Docker firewall (DOCKER-USER chain) and will not appear in "ufw status".
net-expose.cidr-hint: Leave the source empty to allow any address, or restrict it to a CIDR range like 203.0.113.0/24.
net-expose.close-hint: Enter the same protocol, port and source above to remove an existing opening.
power-mgmt.title: Power management
power-mgmt.description: Hard-drive spin-down, scheduled shutdown & wake, and Wake-on-LAN for this device.
power-mgmt.admin-only: Only an administrator can manage power settings.
power-mgmt.unavailable: Power management is not available on this device yet.
power-mgmt.wsl2-note: This device runs inside WSL2, where power is managed by the Windows host. Spin-down, scheduled shutdown and Wake-on-LAN do not apply here.
power-mgmt.nvme-note: Applies to spinning hard drives (sd*) only. NVMe and SSD drives do not use spin-down.
power-mgmt.schedule-off-note: Scheduling is off by default. When armed, the device powers off at the shutdown time and wakes itself at the wake time.
power-mgmt.test-wake-hint: Run a non-destructive ~3-minute wake test first to confirm this device can wake itself from the RTC alarm before you arm a real schedule.
power-mgmt.lockout-body: Once this device powers off there is no software way to turn it back on. If the scheduled wake fails you will need physical access to power it on again. Only arm this after a successful Test Wake.
power-mgmt.profile.heading: Power profile
power-mgmt.profile.unavailable: Power profiles are not available on this device (the power-profiles daemon is not installed).
power-mgmt.hibernate.heading: Hibernate
power-mgmt.hibernate.na-wsl2: Hibernate is not available: this device runs inside WSL2 and is managed by the Windows host.
power-mgmt.hibernate.needs-swap: Hibernate is not available: it needs persistent swap at least as large as this device's RAM, which is not configured.
power-mgmt.hibernate.na-no-unit: Hibernate is not available on this device: the kernel has no suspend-to-disk support.
power-mgmt.hibernate.note: This is an informational status only. Hibernate is not offered as an action in this version — it would require swap and bootloader changes and is a documented future step.
lan-dns.title: LAN DNS & mDNS
lan-dns.description: Reach this box by its real name on your local network, without going out to the internet.
lan-dns.admin-only: Only an administrator can manage LAN DNS.
lan-dns.unavailable: LAN DNS is not available on this device yet.
lan-dns.no-domain-note: No main domain is configured for this box yet. Set up your domain first so LAN DNS points at a name that already has a valid certificate.
lan-dns.point-router-note: This does not change your LAN automatically. Point your router's DHCP DNS (or individual clients) at this box's IP to use it. LivOS never becomes your only DNS server on its own — if the box goes down your LAN loses DNS, so keep a secondary resolver.
lan-dns.cf-disjoint-note: Independent of Cloudflare / portal mode — enabling this never changes your Cloudflare DNS or portal setup.
lan-dns.mdns-scope-note: .local (mDNS) finds the box only, not individual apps.
webdav.description: WebDAV is an alternative to network sharing that mounts your files over HTTPS.
webdav.credentials-note: Sign in with your own LivOS username and password — the same credentials you use to log in. Every user reaches only their own files.
webdav.https-note: The connection is served over HTTPS through the built-in Caddy reverse proxy, so no extra registry change or configuration is needed.
webdav.windows-step: In File Explorer choose "Map network drive", paste the WebDAV address, and sign in with your LivOS username and password.
webdav.windows-maxpath: Windows limits WebDAV paths to about 260 characters (MAX_PATH); very deep folder trees may not open.
webdav.macos-step: In Finder choose Go → Connect to Server, paste the WebDAV address, and sign in with your LivOS username and password.
webdav.linux-step: Use any WebDAV client (for example rclone, GNOME Files, or Dolphin) with the WebDAV address and your LivOS username and password.
network.title: Network
network.description: Hostname, static IP address & DNS servers for this device.
network.admin-only: Only an administrator can change network settings.
network.unavailable: Network settings are not available on this device yet.
network.wsl2-note: This device runs inside WSL2, where networking is managed by the Windows host. Hostname, static IP and DNS are configured in Windows, not here.
network.confirm-banner: Static IP applied. Reconnect over the NEW address and confirm within 90 seconds, or this device automatically reverts to its previous network configuration.
vpn.title: VPN (Tailscale)
vpn.description: Reach this device securely from anywhere over a private Tailscale network.
vpn.admin-only: Only an administrator can manage the VPN.
vpn.unavailable: VPN is not available on this device yet.
vpn.connecting: Setting up — approve this device on your Tailscale account when the link appears.
vpn.scan-qr: Scan this QR code with your phone, or open the link below, to authorize this device on your Tailscale network.
vpn.magicdns-note: MagicDNS conflict fix applied (accept-dns disabled) — your Cloudflare Tunnel stays connected.
portal.byo.title: Trusted LAN HTTPS (bring your own domain)
portal.byo.description: Serve your box over HTTPS on your local network using a domain you already own on Cloudflare. LivOS creates the DNS record on your zone and Caddy issues the certificate — no data leaves your LAN.
portal.byo.domain.label: Portal domain
portal.byo.domain.help: The name your box will be reached at, e.g. box.example.com. It must be a domain in your Cloudflare account.
portal.byo.zoneId.label: Cloudflare zone ID
portal.byo.zoneId.help: Found on the Overview page of your domain in the Cloudflare dashboard.
portal.byo.apiToken.label: Cloudflare API token
portal.byo.apiToken.help: A token with Zone:DNS:Edit permission for this zone. It is stored only on your box and never leaves it.
portal.byo.hostIp.label: Box LAN IP address
portal.byo.hostIp.help: The local network address of this box, e.g. 192.168.1.20. The DNS record points here.
portal.byo.success: Portal DNS record created. Certificate issuance may take a minute on first connect.
portal.byo.certNote: Live certificate issuance requires ports 80/443 reachable for this name; this may need a one-time check on your network.

public-dashboard.admin-only: Only admins can manage the public dashboard.
public-dashboard.enable.label: Enable public dashboard
public-dashboard.enable.caption: Shows a login-free page at /public listing the apps you pick below — it does NOT make those apps themselves public. Each app stays behind its own login unless you separately publish it.
public-dashboard.apps.heading: Apps to show
public-dashboard.apps.empty: No eligible apps. Only installed global apps can be shown on the public dashboard.

public-dashboard.links.heading: Links
public-dashboard.links.invalid-url: Enter a valid http(s) URL — other links will not be clickable.
public-dashboard.page.not-available-desc: This box has not published a public dashboard.
public-dashboard.page.empty: Nothing has been published here yet.

settings.alert-channels.remove-body: You'll stop receiving alerts on this channel. You can add it again later.
settings.alert-channels.secret-hint-ntfy: Optional access token for a protected ntfy topic. Stored encrypted; never shown again.
settings.alert-channels.secret-hint-webh: The full webhook URL to POST alerts to. Stored encrypted; never shown again.

settings.app-store-preferences.title: App Store Preferences
settings.groups.admin-name-note: Heads up — a group named exactly "admin" grants Gitea admin rights to its members when Gitea SSO is enabled. Pick a different name unless that is intended.
settings.groups.delete-confirm: Delete the group "{{name}}"? This cannot be undone.
settings.groups.description: Organize users into groups for shared access — consumed by app sharing and single sign-on.
settings.groups.name: Name
settings.groups.title: Groups
settings.mcp-control.connect-hint: Point an MCP client (e.g. Claude Desktop or the MCP Inspector) at this endpoint over Streamable HTTP, authenticating with a key you mint below.
settings.mcp-control.enable-description: Runs the loopback control-plane server so a local MCP client can inspect and safely act on this box. Off by default.
settings.mcp-control.keys-description: Keys authenticate the transport only — they grant a bounded, safe tool set (inspect + start/stop/restart) and can never perform destructive actions. Mint one per client and revoke it when done.
settings.mcp-control.minted-once-warning: This is the only time the full key is shown. Copy it now and store it somewhere safe — you will not be able to see it again. If you lose it, revoke this key and mint a new one.
settings.mcp-control.no-keys: No keys yet. Mint one to connect an MCP client.
settings.mcp-control.revoke-body: Revoke "{{name}}"? Any MCP client still using this key will immediately lose access. This cannot be undone.
settings.mcp-control.sub: A native, agent-facing control plane for this box. It exposes a small, safe tool set (inspect apps & system, plus start / stop / restart) to a local MCP client.
settings.mcp-control.title: MCP
settings.mcp-control.warning-exposure: Reaching it from anywhere else is a deliberate step you take yourself — via your own tunnel or reverse proxy. Nothing is exposed to the network by default.
settings.mcp-control.warning-loopback: This server listens on 127.0.0.1 only (loopback). It is reachable solely from this box.
settings.mcp-control.warning-title: Loopback-only, and off unless you turn it on
settings.monitoring.empty: No history yet — metrics are collected once a minute.
settings.monitoring.sub: Historical CPU, memory, disk and network trends, and the thresholds that trigger alerts.
settings.monitoring.thresholds-sub: When a container crosses these, an alert is raised and routed to your configured alert channels.
settings.monitoring.title: Resource
settings.security-advisor.check.admin-2f: An admin account has no two-factor authentication
settings.security-advisor.check.stale-ap: Unused API keys older than 90 days
settings.connectivity.mail-description: Also check that your domain has MX records and reverse DNS. Off by default — only useful if you send mail from this box's domain.
settings.connectivity.no-checks: No checks have run yet. Run a check to see results.
settings.connectivity.note: Checks are read-only — they never change your DNS, certificate, or network settings. An alert is sent only when a check newly fails (not on every run).
settings.connectivity.remedy-cert: The certificate is missing or near expiry. Caddy renews Let's Encrypt certificates automatically — confirm ports 80/443 are reachable so renewal can complete.
settings.connectivity.remedy-dns: Your domain does not resolve as expected. Check the DNS A record points at this box (or your tunnel), and that the record has propagated.
settings.connectivity.remedy-mail: No MX records were found for your domain. Add MX records at your DNS provider if you intend to receive mail.
settings.connectivity.remedy-ports: A required port is not listening. Confirm Caddy is running and your firewall/router forwards ports 80 and 443.
settings.connectivity.remedy-tunnel: The tunnel is configured but not running. Restart the tunnel service, then run the check again.
settings.connectivity.sub: A scheduled read-only check of DNS, ports, certificate, and tunnel health. Alerts you when something that was working breaks.
settings.connectivity.title: Connectivity
settings.security-advisor.note.weak-pass: Password strength cannot be audited retroactively (hashes are one-way) — strength is checked when a password is set, not scanned here.
settings.security-advisor.remediation.en: Enable two-factor authentication for every admin account.
Turn on org-wide 2FA enforcement so members are prompted to enrol.
settings.security-advisor.remediation.fa: Enable fail2ban to block brute-force login attempts.
settings.security-advisor.remediation.ss: Disable SSH password authentication and use keys only.
settings.security-advisor.remediation.st: Revoke API keys that have not been used in over 90 days.
settings.security-advisor.sub: Scheduled vulnerability scans and weak-configuration checks with remediation guidance.
settings.security-advisor.title: Security
settings.security-advisor.trivy-note: Image scans cover container CVEs only, not host or app configuration.
settings.users.quota.help: Set a storage limit for {{name}} in gigabytes. Leave blank or 0 for unlimited. Quotas are soft-enforced and refreshed periodically.
settings.users.quota.label: Storage quota
shut-down.complete-text: You can now unplug your device from the power.
shut-down.confirm.title: Are you sure you want to shut down your Livinity?
shut-down.shutting-down-message: Please do not refresh this page or turn off your Livinity while it is shutting down.
software-update.callout: Please do not refresh this page or turn off your Livinity while it is updating.
software-update.gpu.amd-desc: Grant container access to the AMD GPU (render/video groups + /dev/kfd, /dev/dri) for ROCm-capable apps.
software-update.gpu.amd-ready: AMD ROCm access is configured on this server.
software-update.gpu.amd-restart-note: Group access applies to apps immediately. Restart the server if the GPU still isn't detected.
software-update.gpu.amd-wsl2-unsupported: AMD GPU in WSL2 — ROCm passthrough is experimental and unsupported here. Use a bare-metal Linux install for AMD acceleration.
software-update.gpu.intel-info: Intel GPU detected — used automatically for media apps via /dev/dri. No setup needed.
software-update.gpu.title: GPU acceleration
software-update.gpu.unknown-info: A GPU is present but its vendor could not be determined from inside WSL2. Guided install is unavailable.
software-update.gpu.wsl2-toolkit-desc: Install the NVIDIA Container Toolkit so Docker apps can use your GPU. On WSL2 the Windows driver is already in place — no driver install or reboot needed.
software-update.on-latest: You are on the latest LivOS
software-update.rollback.confirm.body: This restores the previous LivOS code, dependencies, and system service files, then restarts services.
software-update.rollback.confirm.db-chec: Also restore the database to its pre-update snapshot
software-update.rollback.confirm.db-warn: All data written since that update will be PERMANENTLY LOST — users, settings, and app records created after it. The restore is all-or-nothing: if it cannot complete, the database is left untouched.
software-update.rollback.confirm.schema-: The database will NOT be restored — this rollback reverts code only.
software-update.rollback.confirm.title: Roll back to {{name}}?
software-update.rollback.description: Restore the previous version if this update caused problems.
software-update.title: Software update
storage.drive-health.title: Drive health
storage.encryption.description: Passphrase-locked folders. A locked folder stays encrypted on disk until you unlock it with its passphrase.
storage.encryption.passphrase-hint: At least 8 characters. This is the only way to unlock the folder — it is never stored.
storage.encryption.recovery-key-warning: Save this recovery key now. It is shown only once and is the only way to recover the folder if you forget the passphrase.
storage.encryption.title: Encrypted folders
storage.encryption.path-hint: Absolute host path — must live under /opt/livos/data (e.g. /opt/livos/data/users/<you>/Secret). This is an admin operation.
storage.encryption.lock-body: Locking re-encrypts the folder. Its files stay on disk but are unreadable until you unlock it again.
storage.encryption.busy: The folder is in use (a file is open). Close it and try again.
storage.disk-encryption.title: Encrypted disks
storage.disk-encryption.description: Encrypt a whole spare internal disk with LUKS2. After a reboot it stays locked until you unlock it with its passphrase — nothing unlocks automatically.
storage.disk-encryption.wsl2-unavailable: Encrypting whole disks isn’t available on this kind of system.
storage.disk-encryption.cannot-list: Can’t read the disks right now, so none are offered for encryption.
storage.disk-encryption.none-eligible: No spare empty disk is available to encrypt.
storage.disk-encryption.busy: The disk is in use. Close anything using it and try again.
storage.disk-encryption.erase-warning: ALL data on this disk will be erased. This cannot be undone.
storage.disk-encryption.typed-confirm-la: Type the disk name to confirm
storage.disk-encryption.passphrase-hint: At least 12 characters. This is how you unlock the disk — it is never stored.
storage.disk-encryption.recovery-key-war: Save this recovery key now. It is shown only once and can unlock the disk if you forget the passphrase.
storage.disk-encryption.no-recovery: If both the passphrase and the recovery key are lost, this disk cannot be recovered — there is no backdoor.
storage.disk-encryption.recovery-key-sav: Type “{{phrase}}” below to confirm you have stored it somewhere safe.
storage.disk-encryption.unlock-body: Enter the passphrase or recovery key for this disk.
storage.folder-quota.title: Folder quotas
storage.folder-quota.description: Set a size limit on a shared folder. By default you only get a warning near the limit; turn on blocking to refuse writes once it is reached.
storage.folder-quota.hard-block-help: When on, writes are refused once the folder reaches its limit. When off, you only get a warning.
storage.folder-quota.remove-body: This removes the size limit on this folder. The files themselves are not changed.
storage.usb-import.title: USB auto-import
storage.usb-import.enable-label: Copy files when a USB drive is plugged in
storage.usb-import.enable-hint: When on, inserting a USB stick or SD card copies its contents into the folder below. The original files on the drive are never moved or deleted.
storage.usb-import.destination-hint: Each insert creates a new date-stamped subfolder here, so nothing is ever overwritten.
storage.usb-import.destination-required: Choose a destination folder before turning this on.
storage.usb-import.destination-invalid: That folder can't be used. Pick a folder inside your files that you can write to.
storage.usb-import.remove-body: This deletes the auto-import rule. Files that were already copied are not changed.
storage.usb-import.empty: No auto-import rule yet. Choose a folder to copy inserted drives into.
storage.usb-import.owner-missing: The user this rule belongs to ({{user}}) no longer exists, so it won't run. Remove it or recreate it.
